Direct Mail Strategy for Lawrence Hearing

Lawrence Hearing · Orange County, NY · Healthcare

Adults 55+

Oversized Postcard

Orange County, NY
Area

The Challenge

Lawrence Hearing, an audiology practice in Orange County, needed to grow their patient base in a competitive healthcare market. They had previously relied on physician referrals and wanted to add direct-to-consumer marketing to reach adults over 55 who may be experiencing hearing loss but had not yet sought treatment.

Our Solution

Cornerstone developed a targeted direct mail campaign using purchased data lists filtered for age (55+), household income, and homeownership in the Orange County area. We designed a professional oversized postcard highlighting free hearing assessments with a clear call-to-action. The campaign was repeated quarterly to reinforce awareness and build familiarity with the practice.

The Results

Lawrence Hearing reported a measurable increase in new patient appointments following each mailing. The quarterly cadence helped establish consistent brand recognition in the community. The direct mail program became a core part of their marketing strategy, complementing their existing referral network with a reliable patient acquisition channel.

Background

Lawrence Hearing is an independent audiology practice serving Orange County, New York. Like many healthcare providers, their patient acquisition had historically relied on physician referrals — ENTs, primary care doctors, and geriatricians would refer patients with suspected hearing loss. While referrals remained a reliable channel, the practice wanted to expand by reaching adults who might be experiencing hearing loss but had not yet visited a doctor about it. This is a large and underserved population: studies show that the average person with hearing loss waits 7-10 years before seeking treatment. Direct-to-consumer marketing through direct mail offered a way to reach these individuals proactively — prompting them to take action rather than waiting for a medical referral. The competitive landscape in Orange County includes national hearing aid chains (Miracle-Ear, HearingLife) with substantial advertising budgets, making differentiation and consistent local presence essential for an independent practice.

Strategy & Execution

Targeted Data List Development

We sourced compiled consumer data targeting adults aged 55 and older within Orange County ZIP codes, filtered for homeownership (a proxy for financial stability and established community residency) and specific household income thresholds. The age and income filters were designed to reach the demographic most likely to need hearing services and most able to invest in hearing aids, which typically cost $2,000-$6,000 per pair. Every list was NCOA-processed for current addresses.

Oversized Postcard Design

An oversized 6" x 9" postcard was selected for maximum visibility in the mailbox. The front featured a clean, professional image with a headline addressing common hearing concerns ('Struggling to Hear Conversations in Noisy Places?'). The back detailed the free hearing assessment offer, practice credentials, insurance information, and a prominent phone number. A QR code linked to an online appointment scheduling page.

Quarterly Campaign Cadence

Rather than a single mailing, we established a quarterly campaign schedule. Research in healthcare marketing consistently shows that repetition drives response — the first mailing introduces the practice, the second builds familiarity, and the third and fourth mailings convert. Each quarterly drop used the same general design template with seasonal messaging updates to maintain brand consistency while keeping the content fresh.

List Rotation and Suppression

Each quarter, we rotated portions of the list (introducing new households) while maintaining a core audience that received every mailing. Active patients were suppressed from the list to avoid mailing existing customers. This rotation strategy ensured the campaign continuously reached new prospects while reinforcing awareness with prior recipients who had not yet responded.

Design Approach

Healthcare direct mail walks a fine line between professional credibility and approachable warmth. The design avoided clinical, sterile imagery in favor of lifestyle photography showing active, engaged adults — the goal was to associate hearing treatment with improved quality of life rather than medical intervention. The practice's credentials (state licensure, professional affiliations, insurance acceptance) were prominently displayed to build trust. Typography was deliberately large and high-contrast — the target audience may have vision limitations alongside hearing concerns. The free hearing assessment offer was positioned as a low-risk, no-obligation entry point. Orange County location details (address, cross streets, parking information) reduced friction for older adults unfamiliar with the practice.

Postal Strategy

The quarterly mailings used USPS Marketing Mail (Standard) to minimize postage costs on the targeted list. Marketing Mail rates for presorted postcards are significantly lower than First-Class — an important consideration for a campaign designed to run four times per year. While Marketing Mail delivery takes 7-14 business days compared to 2-3 days for First-Class, the longer delivery window was acceptable because hearing assessment is not time-sensitive — there is no urgent deadline driving response. The presort processing maximized postal discounts within the Orange County distribution area.

Key Takeaways

Quarterly repetition was the single most important factor in campaign success. Healthcare decisions — especially elective ones like hearing assessment — are considered purchases. Patients need multiple touches before they act. The first mailing plants the seed; subsequent mailings convert it.

The 55+ age targeting proved significantly more effective than broader age ranges. Response rates from the 55-75 demographic were substantially higher than from younger or older segments, confirming that this age range represents the sweet spot for hearing services marketing — old enough to experience age-related hearing changes, young enough to be active and motivated to address them.

The free hearing assessment offer was critical to driving response. Hearing aid purchases involve significant cost and commitment — a free, no-obligation assessment removes the initial barrier. Once patients experience the assessment and understand their hearing loss, conversion to hearing aid purchase follows naturally.

Direct mail complemented, rather than replaced, physician referrals. Many patients who responded to the postcard mentioned they had been meaning to get their hearing checked but had not gotten around to scheduling through their doctor. The direct mail campaign accelerated a decision that was already forming.

Industry Context

Healthcare direct mail is one of the most regulated and highest-ROI applications of targeted mailing. HIPAA does not restrict outbound marketing to prospective patients (only the use of existing patient health information for marketing purposes), so targeted list mailings to demographically appropriate audiences are fully compliant. The lifetime value of a hearing aid patient is substantial — initial fitting, follow-up adjustments, annual check-ups, and eventual replacement after 5-7 years create a long-term revenue relationship. This high lifetime value makes the cost-per-acquisition through direct mail extremely attractive, even at modest response rates. Many audiology practices and healthcare providers across the Hudson Valley use Cornerstone for similar targeted campaigns.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is healthcare direct mail HIPAA compliant?
Yes. HIPAA restricts the use of protected health information (PHI) — existing patient records — for marketing purposes. However, outbound marketing to prospective patients using commercially available demographic data (age, location, homeownership) does not involve PHI and is fully compliant. Cornerstone's data lists are sourced from compiled consumer data, not medical records.

What response rate should a healthcare practice expect from direct mail?
Targeted healthcare direct mail typically generates a 0.5-2% response rate, with audiology and dental practices often at the higher end due to the tangible, action-oriented nature of the offer (free assessment, free exam). At Lawrence Hearing's campaign cost-per-piece and the lifetime value of a hearing aid patient, even a 0.5% response rate generates a strong ROI.

How does direct mail compare to digital advertising for healthcare practices?
Direct mail reaches a demographic (adults 55+) that is significantly less active on social media and less likely to click digital ads than younger populations. For practices targeting older adults, physical mail delivers higher engagement rates than Facebook or Google display ads. Additionally, healthcare keywords are among the most expensive in digital advertising — direct mail often achieves a lower cost-per-lead.

Can Cornerstone handle mailings for multi-location healthcare practices?
Yes. We can produce variable-data mailings where each piece is customized for the nearest practice location — showing that location's address, phone number, and provider name. The mailing list is segmented by geography so each recipient receives information about the most convenient location.
